text:
maria (People Ops): Quick manager pack to paste into 1:1s and final reviews — 3 ready-to-go feedback snippets, 4 self-review prompts, a mini calibration rubric, and example OKR phrasing. Use as copy/paste or adapt. Link: https://intranet.redwood/team/people-ops/feedback-pack

alex (Eng Manager): this is awesome, thanks. can you show a short example for a mid-senior IC who needs focused improvement on scope?

maria (People Ops): sure — added below. TL;DR templates are intentionally concise (one paragraph) so managers can paste into reviews or Slack.

sam (People Ops): reminder: use the "Start / Stop / Continue" section in performance docs if you want structured follow-ups. people-ops-bot will create a task if you react with :todo:.

maria (People Ops): MANAGER SNIPPET A — praise + growth (for strong performers)
- "[Name] consistently delivers high-quality results, particularly on [project]. They show strong ownership and mentor others effectively. To level up further, I recommend broader cross-team initiatives and taking lead on 1 strategic roadmap item next quarter.
Suggested next steps: nominate for ownership of [initiative], and schedule monthly syncs to unblock dependencies."

maria (People Ops): MANAGER SNIPPET B — redirect with clear expectation (for missed scope/delivery)
- "[Name] has solid technical skills, but recently we’ve seen a pattern where larger projects miss scope or timeline. I want to be explicit about the expectation: for projects of this size, please run a 30/60/90 plan with milestones and risk flags, and share it in our weekly planning channel. We’ll pair on the first project plan to make sure prioritization and stakeholder alignment are clear.
Suggested measure: hit milestone cadence for the next 2 projects; we’ll reassess after."

maria (People Ops): MANAGER SNIPPET C — career conversation starter (for developmental coaching)
- "I appreciate your contributions on [X]. I’d like to talk about the next role you’re aiming for and what gaps to close. Specifically, let’s focus on stakeholder influence, cross-team visibility, and shipping larger scoped work. Over the next 6 months, let’s set 2 concrete stretch goals with measurable outcomes (e.g., lead a cross-team launch, drive a 10% performance improvement)."

maria (People Ops): EXAMPLE for mid-senior IC with scope issues (alex asked):
- "Alex, over the past two quarters, we’ve seen repeated scope creep on features A and B which pushed timelines and increased cross-team rework. You have excellent technical implementation, but to improve impact I want you to: 1) document a 3-point scope baseline before dev starts, 2) list assumptions & unblockers, 3) get +1 engineering review focused on API/contract impacts. We’ll follow this for the next project and revisit in 6 weeks. I’ll support by attending the kickoff and helping with stakeholder alignment."

jon (Product): would be helpful to include a 1-line public praise we can put in #all-hands. any template for that?

maria (People Ops): yes — SHORT PUBLIC PRAISE (one-liner): "Shoutout to [Name] for shipping [impactful outcome], which improved [metric] by [X%]—thanks for driving this across teams! :tada:"

maria (People Ops): SELF-REVIEW PROMPTS (paste into the self-review form):
1) "Top 2 accomplishments this cycle and the measurable impact (numbers preferred)." 
2) "One decision you made that didn’t go as planned — what did you learn and what would you change?" 
3) "Where do you want to grow next (skills, scope, influence)? Give 2 concrete objectives and how the manager can help." 
4) "Quick feedback for your manager: what should they start/stop/continue to better support you?"

sam (People Ops): calibration mini-rubric (use in calibration meetings) — 3 axes, single-sentence anchors:
- Impact: Low = "completed tasks with limited product impact"; Medium = "drives outcomes for their team"; High = "drives cross-team or company-level outcomes".
- Execution & Reliability: Low = "misses commitments often"; Medium = "meets commitments with occasional slippage"; High = "consistently delivers and removes blockers".
- Growth & Leadership: Low = "limited mentorship or initiative"; Medium = "mentors peers and influences product decisions"; High = "shapes roadmap and develops others".
Use these to map to a 1-5 calibration score during review syncs.

maria (People Ops): EXAMPLE OKR PHRASES you can copy into team goals:
- "Objective: Improve query latency for embeddings API. Key Result 1: Reduce p95 inference latency from 240ms to 160ms for 512-token requests. Key Result 2: Decrease per-token cost by 12% through batching/quantization." 
- "Objective: Raise model serving reliability. Key Result 1: Achieve 99.95% availability across critical endpoints. Key Result 2: Reduce incident MTTR from 45m to 20m."

alex (Eng Manager): love the OKR latency example — will paste. quick Q: any suggested wording when a peer asks for soft feedback in public?

maria (People Ops): quick script: "Thanks for asking — I can share quick notes in DM, or if you want public praise I can pin a short highlight in the channel. For developmental feedback, I prefer DM first so we can be specific and constructive."

jon (Product): tagging design managers — these templates are handy. can people-ops add a tiny doc with examples by role levels?

maria (People Ops): yes — we’ll draft level-specific snippets (IC2, IC3, Senior, Staff) and post next week in the People Ops docs. react with :heart: if you want us to prioritize a staff-level pack first.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: performance docs due in 2 weeks for Q2 cycle. Use /submit-review to upload drafts.

maria (People Ops): thanks all — ping me if you want a Google Doc copy to customize for your team.

alex (Eng Manager): thanks again, will use these in 1:1s later today.
